title: Evaluate the inner value
text: First, calculate the inner value: what is $$\sin\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)$$

subHints.title: Remember the range
subHints.text: The range of $$\arcsin$$ is $$\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right].$$ It cannot return a value like $$\frac{4\pi}{3}.$$

subHints.title: Connection to the unit circle
subHints.text: Recall that $$\sin\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)$$ represents the $$y$$ coordinate of a point on the unit circle at the angle $$\frac{4\pi}{3}.$$

subHints.title: Find equivalent angle geometrically
subHints.text: The principal range of $$\arcsin$$ is $$\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right], $$ which is the right half of the unit circle. To find an angle in this range that has the same $$y-$$ coordinate as $$\frac{4\pi}{3}, $$ extend a horizontal line straight from that point into Quadrant IV. It hits the right half of the circle at $$\frac{-\pi}{3}.$$ \n\n##figure1.gif##

title: Remark
text: You might be tempted to give $$\frac{5\pi}{3}$$ as your answer since it has the same sine value as $$\frac{\left(-\pi\right)}{3}$$, but $$\frac{5\pi}{3}$$ is outside the restricted domain of arcsin, so it cannot be returned.
